definition: In this historical source, a natural group means a group joined by family relationship rather than by an arranged household role. It refers especially to parents and children, and in a wider sense can include grandparents, grandchildren, and other relatives.

provenance.revision: 1901 New York Macmillan original; archive index checked 2026-10-18
provenance.scope: Source record Family; pinned source text

reasons: The contrast with an 'arranged household role' is not supported by the source packet; the passage defines family as a natural group and separately notes a household as partly natural, partly artificial, but does not frame the term in terms of an arranged role.
The definition adds an interpretive gloss ('joined by family relationship') that is acceptable, but the unsupported contrast makes the overall sense exceed the packet’s wording.

The packet does not support the claim that a natural group is “joined … rather than by an arranged household role”; it only contrasts “natural” (family) with “artificial” elements in a household, explicitly including “servants.”

The packet supports that “natural group” can mean father, mother, and children, and more broadly includes grandparents/grandchildren/relatives, but the provided definition adds wording (“arranged household role”) not present in the supplied text.
